Subject: MAP: cost cross-test — batching vs prefetch impact on tokens/$ and close timeline

John — thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, the MAP close is gated on two cost checkpoints: tokens/$ (burst and steady-state) and the effectiveness of prefix caching/prefetch under your traffic mix.

Quick proposal to keep momentum and unblock the SOW: run a short cross-test so we can validate assumptions in the MAP econ section (attached v2). High-level plan: 
- Day 0 (you): provide 48 hours of anonymized sampling logs (route-level qps, avg prompt length, percent of repeated prefixes).
- Day 1–3 (us): run two experiments in your dev namespace:
  1) Batching sweep: evaluate latency vs cost for batch sizes [1,4,8,16] with concurrency matching your P90 qps.
  2) Prefetch/prefix cache toggle: enable prefix caching for top 10% of repeated prompts and measure token delta + hit rate.
- Day 4: joint readout with SRE + FinOps, update MAP econ table and update tokens/$ used for pricing proposal.

Key asks from PulseHealth: logs + brief list of endpoints that matter for latency SLOs. From our side we will provide scripts and a prebuilt benchmarking container and an initial estimate in the attached spreadsheet.

Can you confirm we have permission to run in a scoped dev project? Also please confirm the earliest window you can share the logs — ideally within next 48 hours so we can align the readout before your internal procurement review next week.

Thanks,
Mina

Internal ask (short):
- Rishi: can you provide a quick fallback pricing band we can offer if caching reduces tokens/$ by >15%? Procurement will likely ask for a scoping clause (example: if cache hit rate > X% then price moves to Y). Need a templated fallback and a suggested limit to include in the MAP.
- Kimberly: can you draft the exact experiments we'll run (batch sizes, concurrency, how we measure token delta and hit-rate), plus the metrics we should capture (tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit_rate, p50/p95 latency, cost_per_1m_tokens). Attach the prefetched benchmark script and expected runtime.

Initial notes (my thinking):
- Use a 72-hour window for the cache experiment to stabilize hit-rate; batching sweep can be quicker (24–36 hours).
- Measure both absolute tokens saved and end-to-end latency impact; procurement cares about cost but SRE cares about tail latency. We must capture both and show tradeoffs.
- For the MAP acceptance gate propose: tokens/$ delta validated AND no >10% regression on P95 latency on any critical endpoint for at least 48 hours.

Attaching the v2 econ sheet (pulsehealth_map_econ_v2.xlsx) — it has a baseline tokens/$ assumption at 0.0009 USD per token and an optimistic caching case at 0.00075 USD per token (these are placeholders pending the cross-test).

On timing: John's team can deliver logs by Thu 11:00 PT if we push the addendum today. If we kick off Thu afternoon, we can have readout Mon/Tue and close the MAP before their procurement sync on Wed. Tight but doable.

Thanks — please reply with the fallback pricing band and the experiment spec so I can finalize the MAP and send the addendum.

Mina / Rishi — quick experiment spec and gating language below. John — copying you so you're aligned with what we'll run.

Experiment spec (dev project, scoped infra with feature flag):
1) Batching sweep (24–36h): run controlled load at three concurrency bands (P50 qps, P90 qps, P95 qps). For each band test batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16. Collect per-route: tokens_in, tokens_out, avg_generation_tokens, cost_estimated (using current pricing), p50/p95 latency.
2) Prefetch/prefix cache (72h): enable prefix caching for the top 10 endpoints by volume. Track: cache_hit_rate (prefix hits / requests), tokens_saved = baseline_tokens_out - cached_tokens_out, end-to-end latency distribution. We'll also run a short mixed workload (50% cached, 50% cold) to model real traffic variability.

Metrics to capture (dashboard-ready):
- tokens_in (sum)
- tokens_out (sum)
- cache_hit_rate (percentage)
- tokens_saved (absolute and percent)
- cost_per_1M_tokens (USD)
- p50/p95 latency per route
- error_rate (5xx)

Analysis steps:
- Compute tokens/$ baseline and cached case; report delta % and absolute USD per 1M tokens.
- Quantify latency tradeoffs: if cache increases P95 by >10% on any critical endpoint mark as regression.

Proposed MAP gating language (we can include in the MAP doc):
"MAP economic acceptance: The customer and Redwood will validate tokens/$ under the agreed dev experiments. Acceptance requires: (a) demonstrated tokens/$ delta <= -15% (i.e., caching reduces cost by at least 15%) OR an agreed fallback pricing band is accepted by procurement; AND (b) no >10% regression in P95 latency for critical endpoints during a 48-hour stabilization window. If (a) is met but procurement cannot accept a price adjustment, the parties will default to a pre-agreed conservative price cap (see suggested bands below)."

Suggested fallback pricing bands (Rishi please sanity-check):
- If cache hit rate >= 35% --> offer 12% discount on unit price for first 6 months.
- If cache hit rate >= 50% --> offer 18% discount.
- If caching delivers <15% savings, no discount; procurement keeps baseline pricing.

Rishi: these are starter numbers — if you can run a quick margin check and give a recommended band I'll lock this into the MAP doc.

John: once you confirm dev access and the addendum timing, we'll push the benchmark container and a short readme (scripts + expected outputs).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
